 Attorney General asks Colom to remove AI-generated ads, says it appears to violate state law 
 One ad depicted Cindy-Hyde Smith running from reporters, according to the MSGOP 
 By WLBT Staff Published : Oct. 23, 2026 at 11:28 AM CDT | Updated : Oct. 23, 2026 at 5:11 PM CDT Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google JACKSON, Miss. (WLBT) - On Friday, Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch notified Scott Colom and Scott Colom for Senate to remove recent AI-generated ads posted by the campaign on their social media platforms.
 According to the AG, the video appears to violate State law against the use of political “deepfakes” to influence elections. 
 Fitch asked that the ads be removed by 3 p.m. on Friday, October 23, or else the office may file an injunction as authorized by law, according to a statement. Violations of Section 97-13-47 of the Mississippi Code carry penalties of up to 5 years in prison and/or fines of up to $10,000 if the intent is to “deter any person from voting.”
 This follows a complaint from the Mississippi Republican Party, which sent a letter to Fitch asking the Attorney General to investigate the incident.
 The party claimed the AI clip depicted Sen. Hyde-Smith running from reporters. Democratic analyst Brandon Jones called the legal filing political nonsense.
 AI ad sparks complaint 
 As of Friday afternoon, the AI video appears to have been deleted from the Scott Colom For Senate Facebook page .
